channel.title: World Gold Council Industry Insights
channel.description: Public first listing page; archive and subsequent pages not promised. Publication day omitted if only month is available.

item.title: From mine to market – building a more transparent and trusted gold supply chain
item.description: The commitment to uploading core provenance data onto the Gold Bar Integrity platform will support the integrity of the gold supply chain. This will not only help anybody who is looking to purchase this gold to have confidence that they can do so in line with their responsible sourcing commitments, but also underpin the creation of digitalised gold products, a new area of growth and innovation that we at the WGC are very excited about.

item.title: COP30: Reflections After the Dust Settles
item.description: After COP30 closed in Belém, Brazil, the sense of promise that surrounded this ‘Implementation COP’ (also referred to, somewhat optimistically, as the ‘COP of Truth’ ) was quickly tempered by reality. The final communique was, frankly, disappointing - ambitious language gave way to compromise, with the hoped-for clarity on fossil fuel phase-out remaining elusive.

item.title: The importance of transparency in building trust in the extractives sector
item.description: This month in Dakar, Senegal, supporters of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) gathered to mark the twentieth anniversary of the initiative and to chart a course for the coming years.

item.title: Why Nature Is Demanding We Pay Attention
item.description: The World Gold Council has, over the last year or so, expanded its research focus from climate change to a much wider environmental lens, recognising that climate stability and socio-economic development are inseparable from healthy ecosystems and biodiversity.

item.title: The role of gold in enabling financial inclusion
item.description: Bringing more people into the financial system is a priority for policymakers across the world.

item.title: Why gold mining companies are signing up to the Gold Bar Integrity Programme
item.description: As 2024 comes to a close, it is encouraging to see the gold industry continuing to make strides towards a more trusted and transparent gold supply chain. To learn more about the importance of the Gold Bar Integrity programme, watch our short film.

item.title: Greater transparency, stronger trust: Building confidence through responsible disclosure
item.description: Trust in gold begins with knowing where the doré comes from, how it has been processed and how it moves through the market. That is why the World Gold Council Board has adopted the Guidance Note on Supply Chain Transparency, a practical step to support clearer, more consistent disclosure of gold doré flows from mined sources.

item.title: Coming Together to Advance Gold's Sustainability Impacts
item.description: The first such event, in 2022, was significant in not only signalling the closer, more co-operative relationship between our two organisations that has developed over recent years, but also the wider move to greater collaboration across the whole gold supply chain.

item.title: A Central Banker's Perspective: Central Bank of Ecuador's gold acquisition program
item.description: The Central Bank of Ecuador (CBE) has strengthened its gold acquisition program over the past three years. The program has made significant progress towards formalisation and access to finance – with good terms – for small-scale and artisanal miners. This important initiative aims to promote sustainable mining practices, foster economic development, enhance financial inclusion within mining communities, and expand the country's international reserves.

item.title: Understanding ASGM: A Vital Segment of the Gold Sector
item.description: ASGM is characterized by low capital intensity and high labor intensity, and it accounts for approximately 20% of global gold supply and supports some 20 million occupations. ASGM is a critical livelihood across rural communities in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, yet about 85% of it operates outside formal regulatory frameworks, making it vulnerable to exploitation by criminal gangs and liable to cause environmental degradation. As the gold price has increased significantly over the last few years, this has become even more of a pressing issue.

item.title: Gold Dealer Assurance Standard: Providing Clarity on Graded Coins
item.description: Since the launch of the Gold Dealer Assurance Standard (GDAS)™, we’ve seen some engaging discussion and debate around how graded coins should be considered within a standard that is designed to support trust, transparency and customer confidence.

item.title: Back from Baku - news from our COP29 correspondent
item.description: I have just returned from almost a week in Baku, Azerbaijan, having attended (and sometimes contributed to) a number of forums and events at (or around) #COP29, the annual focal point of the United Nations’ climate change considerations and negotiations.

item.title: Brazil Takes Initiative to Build a Better Gold Supply Chain
item.description: In September, the Brazilian Forum for Responsible Gold was launched under the leadership of the National Mining Agency. The event was held at the Ministry of Mines and Energy in Brasília and jointly hosted by the Brazilian National Mining Agency together with the World Gold Council and Intergovernmental Forum on Mining.

item.title: Raising the bar on trust and transparency in the retail gold market
item.description: Over the years, the World Gold Council has been working to enhance trust and transparency across the gold market – through a number of different projects and initiatives.

item.title: Gold247 Update: Creating the blueprint for digitalised gold
item.description: Here at the World Gold Council, we are working to ensure gold, which has been an integral part of financial systems for hundreds of years, continues to have an important role in the future.

item.title: Artisanal and small-scale gold mining: a vital source of gold supply
item.description: Artisanal and small scale gold mining is a significant and growing source of gold supply, but remains difficult to measure. The World Gold Council is working with partners to improve estimates of ASGM production, deepen understanding of this diverse sector, and build a more complete picture of the global gold market. Better data can also support broader efforts to enhance responsible sourcing and traceability.

item.title: Understanding the Global Illicit Gold Economy
item.description: In June, the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), a research institute focused on global security, conflict and development, published a new report that took an in-depth look at 10 gold-producing countries across Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia to examine the factors shaping global security, governance and economic dynamics across these gold-producing regions.

item.title: Expanding the trusted gold ecosystem; building a more transparent and trusted gold supply chain
item.description: The gold industry is going through a period of significant change, including the important steps that are being taken by gold miners to disclose the refineries to which they send their gold.

item.title: From Principles to Practice: Ensuring a Responsibly Sourced Gold Supply
item.description: Our first webinar in our Responsible Gold Mining series discussed how can the gold sector translate widely accepted principles into real‑world practice, across both artisanal and small‑scale mining (ASM) and large‑scale mining (LSM).

item.title: Event Recap: From Resource to Reserves: the Role of Central Banks in Addressing Artisanal Small-scale Gold Mining
item.description: In October, leaders from central banks, government agencies, and development organizations convened in Washington D.C. to explore how central banks can play a transformative role in formalizing artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) and strengthening domestic gold markets.
